title: Why might different objects get different number names?
description: A group of people on a Pacific island use a different sequence of number names for each kind of object. The video thinks about what is counted, how it comes, and what the listener needs to know, and checks each reason against the question.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number name can carry more than the number, such as how a thing is grouped. This is an open question, so accept any sensible reason. Watch for answers that give a reason but do not explain why the names differ.

source: Figure it Out (early number systems, question 1)
video_script.why: The child uses the idea that a number name follows a group size, as in the Gumulgal names, to give reasons for separate sequences of names.
video_script.substitution: Ask what is counted, how it comes, and what the listener must know, then test each reason against the question.
video_script.anchor: three kinds of objects, each with its own row of number names under it
video_script.payoff_line: Each kind of object is grouped in its own way, and its name tells which kind

final_answer.value: Open answer: for example, each kind of object is grouped or traded in its own way, and the name also tells what is being counted
final_answer.spoken: for example, each kind of object is grouped or traded in its own way, and the name also tells what is being counted

hold_back: Open answer: for example, each kind of object is grouped or traded in its own way, and the name also tells what is being counted
never_show: the answer card before the last beat of the board solution
maths_rules: a number name can follow a group size, as the Gumulgal names follow groups of 2
things that come in bunches or pairs may be easier to count in their own groups
a separate sequence of names also tells the listener what kind of object is meant
check: a good reason explains why one number gets a different name for each kind of object
video_script.design: One idea: a number name can carry the grouping of the thing counted. The three rows of names stay on the stage and each step points at one reason. Any sensible reason is welcome.
